items.summary: Stocks and futures rose after Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh refrained from supporting tighter monetary policy despite recent inflation data. Traders reduced bets on an October rate hike from over 25% to 15%. The dollar edged lower while gold and Asian equities gained. Analysts noted the market rebound may depend on broader participation beyond technology stocks.
items.title: Markets Rise as Fed Chief Warsh Avoids Rate Hike Commitment

items.summary: UBS is evaluating potential moves abroad, including shifting its headquarters or merging with another bank, should new Swiss banking rules prove intolerable. Sources indicate the bank is considering options like acquiring US banks or being taken over. While UBS states it does not comment on speculation, it views the proposed capital requirements as excessive and harmful to its competitiveness.
items.title: UBS Explores Relocation Options Amid Potential Swiss Regulatory Changes

items.summary: NVIDIA and AI4Bharat have released Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1, a dataset comprising approximately 2.8 trillion tokens across 22 Indian languages. The corpus includes 2,601.0 billion native-script tokens and 224.6 billion romanized tokens, generated using an open pipeline that translates English documents and applies quality checks. Mitesh Khapra of AI4Bharat noted that Indian language technology trails English due to data scarcity, a gap this release aims to fill. The synthetic data complements natural text to improve models in technical reasoning and code generation. NVIDIA and AI4Bharat plan to continue building on this corpus for future Nemotron models. The release also includes a technical report and a companion Indic report detailing evaluation results and generation methods.
items.title: NVIDIA and AI4Bharat Release Large Indic Pretraining Corpus

items.summary: Databricks describes how its AI Runtime (AIR) infrastructure supports the company's research team in developing and evaluating new AI techniques. The team uses AIR to manage hundreds of parallel workstreams, scale to large training workloads, and adapt to agent-led training. AIR provides built-in GPU resiliency, fast iteration capabilities through the AIR CLI, and seamless access to research data stored in Unity Catalog. The infrastructure is particularly suited for agent-driven research, where the number of training jobs has grown significantly. Databricks states that AIR allows researchers to focus on model development rather than infrastructure management.
items.title: Databricks AI Runtime Supports Research and Agent-Driven Workflows

items.summary: NVIDIA has released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open multimodal agent model designed for enterprise use. The 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model activates 12B parameters per token and supports inputs including text, images, documents, and video up to two minutes long. NVIDIA states the model achieves up to 5x higher single-GPU throughput than open peers and scores 89.90 on the GPQA-Diamond benchmark. Weights are available under the OpenMDW-1.1 license, with deployment options on various hardware configurations including DGX Spark and H200 systems.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Open Multimodal Agent Model Nemotron 3.5 Super VL

items.summary: Atlassian constructed a security lakehouse on Databricks using the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) to resolve fragmented logging formats from its 350,000 customers. Senior Security Logging Engineer Zachary Schmerber explained that the initiative addressed varied timestamps and proprietary schemas, enabling the processing of 44 billion daily events. The team embedded the OCSF schema into Go structs, a method Schmerber calls 'TypeGo,' to ensure compile-time correctness and reduce AI hallucinations. Jordan from the Detection and Response team noted that standardization allowed the migration from one-to-one alerts to a signal-based methodology. Performance improved by 95% for representative queries after optimization.
items.title: Atlassian Builds OCSF Security Lakehouse on Databricks to Standardize Data

items.summary: BeyondTrust warned customers to patch a critical flaw in its Remote Support software, which has been exploited since late August by actors including Armory Castle and Silk Typhoon. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-102764, allows unprivileged attackers to perform file operations on unpatched appliances. While BeyondTrust patched SaaS customers on October 8, self-hosted installations require manual updates. Mandiant and other researchers report that the flaw grants root access and enables lateral movement.
items.title: BeyondTrust Warns of Exploited Zero-Day Flaw in Remote Support

items.summary: Tesla has re-unveiled its next-generation Roadster, a vehicle originally announced in 2017 that was intended to dominate gasoline-powered sports cars. The company demonstrated the car performing stunts such as driving upside down, executing a kickflip, and accelerating from 0 to 60 mph in under one second. Elon Musk stated the car could fly, attributing these capabilities to a multi-mode suction system and cold gas thrusters. The article notes that while the demo appeared impressive, the physics of the thrusters and the high downforce numbers claimed by Tesla raise questions about practicality and accuracy. The author suggests the thrusters may serve as party tricks rather than genuine performance enhancers for standard driving. The new model is expected to have a range of over 300 miles and will be offered in Performance, Thrust, and Rocket trims, with the Rocket version being the only one certified for flight. The article concludes by questioning the real-world usability of such technology on public roads.
items.title: Tesla Unveils New Roadster With Flying Claims And Thruster Tech

items.summary: Tesla unveiled a new version of its next-generation Roadster featuring design elements from the Cybertruck and cold-gas thrusters enabling jumps and flips. The vehicle offers three trims: Performance, Thrust, and Rocket, with acceleration times ranging from under 1.6 seconds to under 0.59 seconds. While the base model retains road legality, the Thrust and Rocket versions are invite-only and not approved for public road use. Tesla reopened reservations at $50,000, though no specific price or production date was set, with Musk citing 2028. The new design reduces range to over 300 miles compared to the original 620-mile promise.
items.title: Tesla Unveils Cyberfied Roadster with Thrusters and Stunt Capabilities

items.summary: American Electric Power (AEP) announced plans for a $4 billion, 702-MW Bloom Energy fuel cell plant in Wyoming to supply Google, alongside a purchase of 190 MW of Mainspring Energy linear generators under an agreement for up to 1.6 GW through 2034. The Wyoming plant is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2028. AEP stated the project aims to deliver reliable, near-zero-emissions power. The Mainspring agreement is described as the largest procurement of linear generators to date. AEP Chairman Bill Fehrman noted the project demonstrates new opportunities to meet evolving energy needs.
items.title: AEP Announces $4 Billion Fuel Cell Plant for Google and Mainspring Generator Deal

items.summary: Eight major Chinese polysilicon manufacturers met in Hangzhou to discuss curbing below-cost sales and reducing output due to persistent overcapacity. They proposed a tax-inclusive minimum price of CNY 43,000 per metric ton, reflecting production costs. However, no binding quotas or enforcement mechanisms were disclosed, and futures prices remain well below the proposed floor as weak demand and rising inventories continue to pressure the market.
items.title: Chinese Polysilicon Producers Discuss Price Floor Amid Oversupply

items.summary: China TOPCon solar cell prices declined following the Golden Week holiday, with M10 and 210R formats falling 0.86% and 0.66% respectively to $0.0463/W and $0.0454/W. Industry sources attribute the drop to weakening overseas demand and potential U.S. stockpiling restrictions. While the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association forecasts gradual utility-scale demand recovery, market participants question its sustainability. Meanwhile, manufacturers in Hangzhou discussed setting price floors for polysilicon and modules, though these agreements lack legal enforceability. China added 97.19 GW of capacity in the first eight months of the year, down significantly from the previous year.
items.title: Chinese Solar Cell Prices Drop as Industry Considers Price Floors

items.summary: Global fuel oil supply is shrinking while shipping demand remains robust, suggesting further supply pain. Middle East exports are at least 800,000 tons a month lower than pre-war levels, and Russian refinery losses add another 1 million tons monthly. Spot market premiums have surged to nearly $50 per ton from $5.10. Refiners in Asia are snapping up cargoes amid disruption in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz.
items.title: Global Fuel Oil Shortage Deepens Amid Middle East and Russia Supply Collapse

items.summary: Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster demonstrated flight capabilities, claiming 0-100 km/h in 0.81 seconds. Three variants—Performance, Thrust, and Rocket—are expected by 2028, with booking details provided in Indian Rupees. Regulatory approval for road use remains pending.
items.title: Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster showcases flight capabilities with new variants

items.summary: In an interview with TIME, Apple marketing chief Greg Joswiak stated that Apple Intelligence is designed for "everyday people" rather than hardcore enthusiasts pursuing superintelligence. He described the technology as a practical tool for ordinary users, explicitly noting that while they appreciate die-hard AI believers, such ambitious possibilities are not Apple's target. Joswiak emphasized that the company's AI ambitions remain people-centric.
items.title: Apple's Greg Joswiak Clarifies AI Focus on Everyday Users

items.summary: Current and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for Anthropic's upcoming IPO, citing a slowdown in revenue growth. While the company reported a 45% revenue jump to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, investors expressed disappointment over the decelerating sequential growth rate compared to the previous quarter. Sources say these concerns come amid broader worries about the ballooning cost of financing AI development.
items.title: Investors Temper Anthropic IPO Valuation Amid Revenue Slowdown

items.summary: CNN, the Financial Times, Axios, and over 400 other global publishers joined Google's AI news program on October 15 to license content for generative AI features. The partnership allows Google to develop new tools while paying participating organizations. Google stated the features will include clear attribution and direct links to sources. CNN CEO David Ellison noted the deal supports the company's strategy to position itself as a technology-driven media business amid declining referral traffic.
items.title: Major Publishers Join Google's AI News Licensing Program

items.summary: The UK stated it is prepared to align its tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles with those of the EU. This move aims to support Brussels as it negotiates with Beijing to narrow the trade gap. European leaders have adopted an aggressive stance to protect native businesses from a surge in Chinese imports, which policymakers blame for job losses. Brussels is now considering checks on Chinese chemicals and machinery.
items.title: UK and EU consider coordinating tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles

items.summary: The UK stated it is prepared to align its tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles with those of the EU. This move aims to support Brussels as it negotiates with Beijing to narrow the trade gap. European leaders have adopted an aggressive stance to protect local businesses from a surge in Chinese imports, which policymakers blame for job losses. Meanwhile, Brussels is considering checks on Chinese chemicals and machinery.
items.title: UK Signals Potential Tariff Alignment with EU on Chinese EVs

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey is expected to increase taxes on UK banks in the October budget to address fiscal damage from the Middle East war. The move, reported by the Guardian, faces opposition from industry groups concerned about competitiveness.
items.title: Chancellor John Healey poised to raise bank taxes in October budget

items.summary: A reviewer recalls first seeing Ingmar Bergman's 1965 film Persona as a teenager, noting its greatest opening sequence is a rapid-fire montage that defies full understanding. The story follows actress Elisabeth Vogler, who becomes mute after a performance, and her nurse Alma, whose constant talking intertwines with the patient. More than 60 years later, the film remains inexhaustible, intimate, stark, and utterly compelling.
items.title: A Reviewer Reflects on the Enduring Impact of Ingmar Bergman's Persona

items.summary: DeepSeek restored its API and Chat Service at 1:04 p.m. Beijing Time on Thursday following a morning outage affecting three components. The company announced refunds for usage between October 8 and 14 in the form of credit. DeepSeek apologized, launched an investigation, and stated it eliminated single points of dependency to prevent recurrence, though it did not disclose the root cause.
items.title: DeepSeek Restores Services and Announces Compensation Following Outage

items.summary: Elon Musk unveiled the Tesla Roadster, an electric vehicle capable of flight, during a livestreamed event. He demonstrated its capabilities with a ramp launch and a kickflip over other cars. Musk attributed the vehicle's flight ability to altitude control thrusters and a fan suction system developed with SpaceX. The Rocket variant is currently invite-only, with a range exceeding 300 miles and a top speed over 230 mph.
items.title: Elon Musk Unveils Flying Tesla Roadster at Live Event

items.summary: President Xi Jinping opened the 140th China Import and Export Fair in Guangzhou, emphasizing China's commitment to opening up and safeguarding global supply chains. The event coincides with a surge in China's foreign trade, which rose 18.8% year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first nine months of 2026. Xi's letter highlights the fair's 70-year role in promoting trade exchanges. Experts note that intermediate goods and equipment manufacturing drive export growth, while China remains the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years. The fair features over 30,000 exhibitors and 340,000 overseas buyers, showcasing new and green products.
items.title: President Xi Opens 140th Canton Fair Amid Trade Growth

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang called for an open world economy and greater market connectivity at the opening of the 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, in Guangzhou on October 15, 2026. Marking the fair's 70th anniversary, Li described China as both a 'super seller' and a 'super buyer,' highlighting its commitment to integrating domestic and international markets. The event featured 32,000 exhibitors, with green products accounting for a record 26% of exhibits. Li noted that over the past seven decades, the fair has attracted buyers from more than 220 countries and regions, with business deals reaching $1.6 trillion. He emphasized China's role in boosting global purchasing power and supporting industrial growth in developing countries through overseas investment.
items.title: Premier Li Calls for Open World Economy at 70th Canton Fair

items.summary: Autumn blankets vast cotton fields in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, where powerful machines harvest the crop with remarkable efficiency. In 2025, Xinjiang produced 6.165 million tonnes of cotton, accounting for about 23% of the world's total output. Satellite-guided planting, water-saving irrigation, and mechanized harvesting are transforming how this essential crop is grown.
items.title: Xinjiang Cotton Harvest Reaches 6.165 Million Tonnes in 2025

items.summary: Nationals leader Matt Canavan claimed both his party and the Liberals oppose the proposed Australia-EU trade deal, a statement that angered Liberal senators who insist the matter remains unsettled. While Canavan argued the agreement weakens climate policy and harms farmers, Liberal senators told the ABC the deal is better than the status quo and should be adopted. Trade Minister Don Farrell rejected calls to renegotiate, stating the deal is done and that the Nationals would vote against it. A joint parliamentary committee is expected to scrutinise the deal early next year before it is signed. The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry supports ratification, calling it in the national interest despite not being perfect.
items.title: Liberals and Nationals Clash Over Australia-EU Trade Deal

items.summary: Enav announced that faults in Italy's airport data transmission network caused flight delays and cancellations on Friday morning. The national air navigation service provider stated the issue was not a cyber attack. Flow management measures reduced aircraft capacity in Italian airspace starting at 6:00 to ensure operational safety. Delays of up to 60 minutes were reported at Rome, Milan, and Naples airports.
items.title: Italy Airport Network Glitch Causes Flight Delays and Cancellations

items.summary: A study suggests fish in seagrass meadows provide a richer mix of nutrients than those in coral reefs, potentially offering greater food security for coastal communities in Kenya, Tanzania, and Mozambique. Researchers surveyed 40 sites along the East African coastline, finding seagrass fish communities were 1.6 times more nutritionally multifunctional. While coral reefs support greater biomass, seagrass fish could meet significant daily requirements for iron, selenium, and zinc. Lead author Benjamin Jones emphasizes integrating nutritional benefits into conservation policies, though other scientists note methodological limitations and call for further investigation into how these findings translate to reduced malnutrition.
items.title: Study Finds Seagrass Meadows Offer Richer Nutrients Than Coral Reefs

items.summary: Singapore sports coaches report significant income loss due to lesson cancellations and facility closures caused by worsening haze. Senior swim coach Grayson Ong estimates over 80% of his lessons were cancelled in the past one to two weeks. ActiveSG temporarily closed outdoor and non-air-conditioned facilities across most regions as of Friday, Oct 16. Freelance coaches like Priscilla Boon and Timothy Ting face uncertainty regarding class resumption and payment. The National Instructors and Coaches Association urges service buyers to provide fair compensation for last-minute cancellations. Users also express frustration over lack of timely notification regarding facility closures.
items.title: Singapore Sports Coaches Face Income Loss Due to Haze Closures

items.summary: Officials report four deaths and two severe burn injuries among a 12-person crew trapped by smoke and flames in Semeru National Park, East Java. Police are investigating potential negligence. The incident occurs amid a regional haze crisis driven by El Niño, with Indonesia recording 799 hotspots and Malaysia rejecting compensation claims in favor of diplomatic engagement.
items.title: Four Die in Indonesian Wildfire as Haze Crisis Worsens

items.summary: Sources say the U.S. and Myanmar's military-backed government held secret talks in Tokyo last week, marking their second meeting in a month. This reengagement follows the 2021 coup. While earlier discussions in Naypyitaw addressed a detained American businessman and scam centers, the scope of these Tokyo talks remains unclear. Three anonymous sources disclosed the meeting due to its sensitivity.
items.title: U.S. Holds Secret Talks With Myanmar Military in Tokyo

items.summary: Daniel Calvert, formerly of the three-Michelin-starred Sezanne, opened his first independent restaurant, Chez Calvert, in Tokyo's Azabudai Hills complex. The establishment, located in Minato Ward, describes its cuisine as rooted in French traditions while highlighting Japan's seasonal ingredients. The omakase course starts at ¥57,200. Calvert announced the project in July, following his departure from Sezanne in March.
items.title: Chef Daniel Calvert Opens Independent Restaurant Chez Calvert in Tokyo

items.summary: The senior member of the Exclusive Brethren denied knowledge of members volunteering for the Liberal party during the 2025 election. He rejected claims of coordination or funding, stating he did not plan, direct, or fund such activities. While a parliamentary committee hearing saw accusations of religious persecution, the leader maintained his sermon was not a call to action and he had no awareness of its use in election advertising.
items.title: Exclusive Brethren Leader Denies Church Election Involvement

items.summary: Indonesia faces international criticism for its handling of forest fires sending hazardous haze to Malaysia and Singapore. Officials, including President Prabowo Subianto, refuse to apologize, dismissing the crisis as largely natural and citing active firefighting figures that experts argue are misleading. Environmentalists blame inadequate preparedness and decades of forest clearing. While neighboring countries offered assistance, Indonesia has not formally accepted it. The crisis has caused widespread health impacts, with hundreds of thousands of respiratory illness cases recorded in Indonesia and Singapore ranking as the most polluted city globally.
items.title: Indonesia Criticized for Haze Response and Denial of Blame

items.summary: Money transfer firm Wise raised its full-year revenue growth outlook to the upper end of its target range, citing strong customer growth and higher cross-border volumes. While net revenue grew 21% in the second quarter, the cross-border take rate fell to 0.49% as Wise cut prices to attract new customers. The company plans to reapply for a denied national trust bank license.
items.title: Wise Raises Revenue Growth Outlook Amid Cross-Border Volume Surge

items.summary: The UK government announced a ban on pornography depicting strangulation, incest, and related violence, effective from 6 November. This legislation follows a review by Conservative peer Gabby Bertin, who highlighted the real-world dangers of such content. The Justice Minister, Alex Davies-Jones, stated the move aims to prevent the normalization of violence, particularly among young people. Campaign groups welcomed the change, urging strict enforcement.
items.title: UK Government Bans Pornography Depicting Strangulation and Incest From Early November

items.summary: Torrential rain triggered severe flooding near Istanbul, Turkey, on October 15, causing the worst rainfall in 80 years. At least three people died and five remain missing. Officials described the downpour as the heaviest in at least 80 years. Emergency crews worked to clear debris while residents struggled with disrupted services and submerged streets.
items.title: Deadly floods strike Istanbul after worst rainfall in 80 years

items.summary: Local sources reported that Israeli occupiers attacked Palestinian olive pickers in Turmus Ayya, physically assaulting farmers and torching three vehicles on Friday, 16 October 2026. The Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission documented 136 attacks linked to the olive harvest season since October, including beatings, expulsions, and theft. These incidents have intensified since the start of Israel's genocide on Gaza in October 2023.
items.title: Israeli Forces Attack Olive Pickers in Central West Bank

items.summary: A morning briefing on October 16, 2026, reports US President Donald Trump ruling out the use of nuclear weapons against Iran, describing the 'mother of all bombs' as a non-nuclear conventional weapon. Simultaneously, a Saudi-led coalition intercepted a drone over eastern Saudi Arabia. In the US, a shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, resulted in five deaths, including three children and a teacher. Other news includes Brazilian driver Rafael Camara's Formula 1 debut scheduled for 2027, FIFA President Gianni Infantino apologizing over a commercial rights proposal, and the International Energy Agency agreeing to release 100 million barrels of emergency oil stocks.
items.title: Trump Rules Out Nuclear Strike on Iran Amid Global Tensions

items.summary: UK bookstores are scrambling to stock Sally Rooney's novels after her publisher, Faber, stopped distributing them due to Rooney's financial support for Palestine Action, a group banned by the UK government. The ban makes supporting the group punishable by up to 14 years in prison. While some stores rushed to buy remaining stock, distributors had already run out. The Booksellers Association confirmed existing stock can still be sold. The situation has reignited debate over the ban, with the group challenging its proscription in court and the government maintaining that lawful protest remains a democratic right.
items.title: UK Bookstores Scramble as Sally Rooney's Novels Pulled Over Palestine Action Support

items.summary: Indian authorities closed a central park in New Delhi to prevent a rally by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party. The group protests the removal of over 130 million names from voter lists, alleging bias against minorities. While the party demands the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar, police urged caution and cited administrative reasons for the closure. The movement has emerged as a significant political challenge for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
items.title: Indian Authorities Close Park Ahead of Cockroach Movement Rally

items.summary: Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster featuring rocket-style thrusters developed with SpaceX, announcing production will begin in 2028. CEO Elon Musk described the vehicle as an engineering flex with no commercial value, while analysts note its symbolic importance as a halo car. The car demonstrated air maneuvers and high speeds, though Musk downplayed its financial impact. Tesla is shifting focus toward self-driving technology and robotics, with the Roadster serving as a showcase amid declining sales of older models. Reservation deposits range from $50,000 to $250,000, with a base price previously quoted at $200,000.
items.title: Tesla Unveils Flying Roadster with SpaceX Thrusters for 2028 Production

items.summary: Ukrainian officials allege that SpaceX abruptly restricted Starlink services in Ukraine, causing civilian deaths and hindering military operations. While SpaceX CEO Elon Musk distinguishes between commercial Starlink and government-owned Starshield, sources report both were disrupted. The incident sparked debate over who controls access to the technology. A 2022 Reuters report details a specific shutdown in September that affected counteroffensives, though neither Musk nor the US government confirmed deliberate restrictions. SpaceX denies the report's accuracy, citing a commitment to Ukrainian service.
items.title: Ukrainian Officials Blame Musk for Starlink Disruption

items.summary: TCS stated that up to 80 per cent of its new hires will possess digital and AI skills. The company noted that AI-led work now accounts for 10 per cent of revenue and expects this growth to expand profit margins. Executives emphasized that willingness to learn is key for mid-career professionals, while the firm plans to invest in niche talent and partnerships.
items.title: TCS Plans to Hire Digital and AI Talent

items.summary: The Free Press Journal's noon guide presents a digest of top headlines. It reports on a planned protest in Mumbai, Tesla's new flying car, Reliance's response to Musk, Mumbai's air quality, a US arrest, a sprinter's story, a cricket dispute, Apple's foldables, SEBI rule changes, and Navratri details.
items.title: FPJ Quick Take Covers Mumbai Protest, Tesla Car, and More

items.summary: TCS CEO K Krithivasan stated that US government actions against tech firms are driven by local job sensitivities rather than company domicile. He noted TCS applied for only about 10 green cards last year with fewer than 300 H1-B applications. Meanwhile, industry body Nasscom argued immigration and talent mobility are distinct issues. TCS maintains a long-term US strategy with over 30,000 employees, half of whom are locals.
items.title: TCS Says US Tech Actions Driven by Local Job Sensitivities Not Domicile

items.summary: Reliance Industries responded to Elon Musk's remarks regarding Starlink's entry into India, stating it welcomes competition and that all players must abide by Indian laws. Reliance noted that its Jio brand entered the telecom market in 2016 with zero customers but now serves over 530 million. The company emphasized that the government applies the same process to every applicant. Meanwhile, the communications ministry rejected charges of discrimination, calling them baseless.
items.title: Reliance Industries Welcomes Competition and Calls for Starlink to Abide by Indian Laws

items.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus criticized early foldable phones as 'cheap and crappy,' citing durability and crease issues as reasons for Apple's delayed entry. The iPhone Duo, priced at Rs. 2,99,900 in India, begins pre-booking on October 16 with sales starting October 23. Ternus noted that Apple waited years to resolve these technical challenges before launching its own device.
items.title: Apple CEO John Ternus Criticizes Early Foldables as iPhone Duo Pre-Orders Open

items.summary: The Indian rupee gained 20 paise to reach 94.79 against the US dollar on Friday, supported by Reserve Bank of India interventions and a weakening dollar index. However, gains were limited by elevated crude oil prices and early market pressure. The dollar index fell 0.54% to 102, while Brent crude futures dropped 0.54% to $105.35 per barrel.
items.title: Rupee Gains Against Dollar Amid RBI Support and Weak Greenback

items.summary: Microsoft President Brad Smith warned that suspending tech giants from the Green Card program could harm US competitiveness and drive talent abroad. In an interview with Decoded by Politico, he rejected Vice President JD Vance's visa fraud accusations as off base. Smith highlighted the irony of restrictions coinciding with awards to immigrant-founded companies and emphasized the risk of sending top AI engineers to other countries.
items.title: Microsoft President Warns Over Green Card Suspension Impact

items.summary: Reliance Industries stated it welcomes competition but emphasized that all players must abide by Indian laws. This response followed Elon Musk's social media remarks criticizing delays in Starlink's entry into India. Reliance noted that its own Jio satellite services are also awaiting clearances, while the government affirmed its regulatory process is fair and non-discriminatory for all applicants.
items.title: Reliance Industries responds to Elon Musk's criticism of Starlink entry in India

items.summary: Elon Musk demonstrated a flying Tesla Roadster at an event, showcasing its ability to accelerate rapidly and perform stunts using compressed-air thrusters. While Musk stated production is planned for 2028, the company did not announce a price or specific release date. The demonstration highlighted the vehicle's unconventional performance features, though Tesla noted that these capabilities have yet to be established in a production vehicle.
items.title: Elon Musk Unveils Flying Tesla Roadster With Rocket Capabilities

items.summary: Multiple states filed lawsuits accusing OpenAI of allowing ChatGPT to provide dangerous advice and encourage self-harm. Plaintiffs claim the company prioritized profit over safety while misleading users about testing. While OpenAI states its teen version includes protections, critics argue these measures fail to detect minors or prevent harm. The suits join similar actions against other tech giants.
items.title: States Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety Risks to Children

items.summary: Elon Musk and his political committee, America PAC, agreed to settle two class-action lawsuits alleging they defrauded voters in seven swing states by promising a $1 million daily lottery to encourage petition signatures. Plaintiffs claimed the winners were not randomly drawn. While Musk and his team denied wrongdoing, asserting payouts were compensation for spokespeople, the settlement ends the litigation pending court approval. The scheme occurred ahead of the 2024 US presidential election, during which 18 individuals received the prize. Musk, a major Republican donor, faces scrutiny over the legality of such inducements.
items.title: Elon Musk Settles Lawsuit Over Deceptive Election Lottery Scheme

items.summary: Rahul Gandhi questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding the upcoming Mumbai visit of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Gandhi alleged confusion within the external affairs ministry concerning the meeting arrangements. These remarks followed Congress criticism of the Centre's silence on the matter. US Ambassador Sergio Gor noted expectations for External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar to meet Rubio in Mumbai.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Criticizes Modi Over Rubio Visit Confusion Allegations

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah criticized the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government in Punjab regarding law and order. He cited the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa and the death of a father in Dirba who allegedly consumed poison under pressure. Shah stated the Centre will seek answers from the state government over these incidents.
items.title: Amit Shah Demands Answers From Punjab Govt Over Activist Killing

items.summary: Uppal police arrested 33-year-old Pullagura Suryanarayana for creating a fake matrimonial profile and harassing a woman constable from Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh. The accused claimed to be a railway section engineer. After the victim discovered the details were fake, she found he collected Rs. 1.10 lakh and threatened to leak private videos. Police arrested him based on her complaint and sent him to judicial remand.
items.title: Uppal Police Arrest Man for Fake Matrimony Profile and Harassment

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the CJP, stated that businesses suffer when the government shuts down the city, attributing the issue to the shutdown rather than peaceful protests. He spoke as a traders' body complained about the situation.
items.title: CJP's Dipke Says Businesses Suffer When Government Shuts Down City

items.summary: Amid massive protests, the Election Commission announced two moves long demanded by the opposition. It ordered a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states and UTs to enrol new voters. Additionally, the ECI promised to provide political parties with readable PDF copies of final electoral rolls for the first time. These decisions come after criticism regarding the Special Intensive Revision exercise, which excluded over 13 crore voters. The Commission reversed its stance on releasing machine-readable lists, citing previous privacy concerns. Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and P Chidambaram, welcomed the changes while questioning the Commission's motives.
items.title: Election Commission Announces Voter Roll Revisions Amid Protests

items.summary: The FBI extradited Manjeet Singh Bedi, a fraud suspect accused of defrauding the US government of at least USD 600,000 in SNAP benefits, from India to the United States. Bedi, who fled to India after crossing into Canada, will face charges in Washington state. FBI officials credited international partners and public tips for his return.
items.title: FBI Extradits Most Wanted Fraud Suspect Manjeet Singh Bedi From India

items.summary: The Press Council of India (PCI) has issued comprehensive guidelines for journalists covering protests, emphasizing safety and neutrality. The PCI expressed concern over media personnel's safety during unrest. Guidelines mandate visible identity cards, prohibit participation in demonstrations, and advise maintaining distance during tensions. Journalists are warned against touching explosive devices and broadcasting real-time police tactical movements to ensure operational security.
items.title: Press Council of India Issues Safety and Neutrality Guidelines for Journalists Covering Protests

items.summary: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that the Centre will make the West Bengal government the custodian of enemy properties in the state. The move, approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs, aims to use revenue from these assets for local development. West Bengal holds around 4,000 such properties across several districts.
items.title: West Bengal Govt to Custodian Enemy Properties
